product.title: Delivery Empire — Economic Strategy Game
product.summary: A strategy-layer sequel to the delivery business, focused on competition and scale.
product.whatStudentsDo: Students make repeated strategic calls running a delivery operation — pricing against rivals, investing in capacity, absorbing demand shifts — and see the cumulative effect across rounds.

studentDataProfile.notes: State kept in browser localStorage only; no server call observed.

governance.maturityBasis: Runs end-to-end and is publicly reachable. No student-run evidence exists.

health.technicalBasis: Playtested end to end 2026-08-16. The economics content is rigorous — expected value, opportunity cost and comparative advantage tested with real applied arithmetic — but the interaction model is answering questions rather than playing.
knownBlockers: An uncaught error, "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading answer)", fires repeatedly during quick interaction with the quiz — a realistic path for a student who double-clicks.
Twenty-five multiple-choice questions dominate the runtime, bookended by one strategy choice and one crisis decision.

curation.tierBasis: The applied economics content is strong; the interaction is twenty-five multiple-choice questions bookended by two decisions, and a runtime error fires on quick clicking.

provenance.evidence: 101-M3-ECON/index.html <title>DELIVERY EMPIRE | Economic Strategy Game</title>. Repo also holds a 7-section Google Apps Script and a Track 101 xlsx.
openQuestions: Relationship to deliverempire (101-M2-ECON) is unconfirmed — same business theme, possibly a deliberate sequel.
